key_insight: PING uses a physics-informed graph neural network to forecast advection-diffusion on irregular sensor networks, improving cloud-motion and solar power prediction.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate intra-day PV forecasting by fusing ground sensors and satellite cloud data, supporting better grid integration of solar generation.
method: Models advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph.
Adds a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft loss constraint.
Couples the forecasting model with PV power prediction using data fusion from weather stations and satellite imagery.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on synthetic and real datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, with results on par with state-of-the-art models.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the graph and physics discretization match the real sensing geometry, which may be challenging for sparse or noisy sensor networks.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
